# location-picker **Let people pick an exact spot on a map, and get `lat,lng` in your form.** Form-ready map location picker: pan a map under a fixed pin to pick one latitude/longitude. Web component + class, keyless OpenStreetMap by default, Google and MapLibre optional. ![location-picker in a form: an OpenStreetMap map with a fixed red pin on the Eiffel Tower, a search box and a locate button, then a Save button and the value the form submits, location=48.85837,2.294481](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/readme-hero.png) **[Live demo](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/)** · [No-code embed](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/embed/) · [Pick link](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/pick/) · [API reference](docs/api.md) · [For AI agents](#for-ai-agents) · MIT One script tag, no API key, no build step. Put the element inside your form: ```html
``` People pan the map under the pin, search for a place, paste coordinates or tap the locate button (the browser asks for permission only then). On Save, the form posts `location=48.85837,2.294481`, latitude first, like any other field. In JavaScript, read the element's `value` or listen for `change`: `e.detail` has `value`, `lat`, `lng`, `source` and `address`. - **With npm:** `npm i location-picker`, then `import 'location-picker'`. Recipes for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and more: [Frameworks](#frameworks). - **With a coding agent:** `npx skills add cyphercodes/location-picker` adds the location-picker Agent Skill (it also ships in the package, at `node_modules/location-picker/skills/location-picker/SKILL.md`). [llms.txt](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/llms.txt) is the short version of these docs, and [Common mistakes](#common-mistakes) lists the traps. - **Without code:** the [embed generator](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/embed/) writes the snippet for WordPress, Webflow, Squarespace, Shopify or a plain HTML form ([per-platform guide](docs/embed.md)). - **To ask a person:** send them the [pick link](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/pick/). They confirm a point on a map with nothing to install, and you get it back as text they copy to you, an `https://` redirect after their click, or a `postMessage` to your origin ([how it works](#ask-a-person-for-a-location-pick-link)). Made for chat bots, AI agents and support tickets. Try [`/pick/?q=Eiffel Tower`](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/pick/?q=Eiffel%20Tower). ## Why location-picker Use it when a form needs **one precise point**: a store, branch or sensor location in an admin screen, a delivery or pickup pin at checkout, an event venue, the place of a report, a home or work location in a profile. - **A real form field.** `required` validates, form reset works and back/forward navigation restores it. Submit one `"lat,lng"` entry (`name`), separate entries (`lat-name`, `lng-name`), or fill inputs you already have (`lat-input`, `lng-input`). See [Forms](#forms). - **No API key to start.** OpenStreetMap through Leaflet by default; Google Maps or MapLibre when you choose them. The default OpenStreetMap tiles and Photon address search are free public services with no SLA: for production traffic, use your own or a commercial tile server and geocoder ([usage policies](#providers-and-usage-policies)). - **Pan, search, paste or locate.** Arrow keys and Enter work too, and the locate button asks for permission only when clicked. Typed or pasted coordinates jump straight there with no network call: `48.8584, 2.2945`, DMS, `geo:` URIs and Google, OpenStreetMap or Apple Maps links. - **Phone-first when you want it.** [Field mode](#phone-first-field-mode) shows a compact control that opens the map full screen; the value changes only on Confirm. - **Your stack.** Plain HTML forms and server templates (Laravel, Django, Rails), React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid and Preact; jQuery, Livewire, Alpine and htmx through bound inputs. TypeScript types and JSX typings are included. - **No runtime npm dependencies.** Leaflet, MapLibre and the Google Maps types are optional peers. When the page has no Leaflet, it is loaded from jsDelivr ([Install](#install)). - **Clear errors, generated test results.** Every runtime problem has a stable `code` and a one-line fix ([error codes](docs/errors.md)). Browser and device results come from the test matrix: [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). **When not to use it:** drawing shapes, routes or areas; several markers; a full mapping application (use Leaflet, MapLibre or the Google Maps JS API directly); text-only address autocomplete with no map; offline maps; React Native or other native mobile apps. ## Install | How | Use | | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Script tag (no bundler) | `` | | npm | `npm i location-picker`, then `import 'location-picker'` | | npm, class only | `import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core'` (defines no element) | | Upgrading 1.x code | `import locationPicker from 'location-picker/v1'` ([migration guide](docs/migration.md)) | The script tag defines `` and sets `window.LocationPicker` (the class, with every export as a static). `https://unpkg.com/location-picker@3` serves the same file. Keep the `@3`: the unpinned `/dist/location-picker.min.js` path is the frozen v1 file. In ES modules from a CDN, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3/+esm` defines the element too. Leaflet 1.9.4 is loaded on demand from jsDelivr with Subresource Integrity, only when `window.L` is absent. Bundler users can pass their own Leaflet instead (see [the JavaScript class](#javascript-class)). To watch the value change while you try it, here is a complete page: ```html Pick a location

Picked: nothing yet

``` ## How the value works - The picker starts **unset** (`value === ""`) unless you give it a `value`. While unset, the map shows `center` (or a world view) and the pin is dimmed. - The user **commits** a point by panning the map, using the arrow keys, pressing Enter on the map, clicking the confirm button (shown while unset when `center` is set), picking a search result, or locating. `setLocation()` commits too. - Zooming never changes the value: zoom is anchored at the pin. - Every commit fires `input` (final value), then `change`, with `detail.source`: `user`, `api`, `geolocation` or `search`. Live `input` events fire while the user drags. - Writing `el.value = '48.8584,2.2945'` is silent (no events), like a native ``. - The value string is always latitude first, dot decimal, no spaces, rounded to `precision` decimals (6 by default): `"48.85837,2.294481"`. ## Forms The element is form-associated: it validates with `required`, resets with the form and restores on back/forward navigation. Choose what it submits: | Attributes | Submitted entries | | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `name="loc"` | `loc=48.85837,2.294481` | | `lat-name="lat" lng-name="lng"` | `lat=48.85837`, `lng=2.294481` | | `+ address-name="addr"` | `addr=
` (`""` while unknown) | | `lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng"` (bound inputs) | your existing inputs submit themselves; the picker fills them | The recommended server-rendered pattern puts the inputs inside the element. Without JavaScript they are visible and typed by hand; with it they are hidden, filled by the map, and still submitted. Their server values seed the picker, and a form reset brings them back. ```blade

``` ```php // StoreController@update $data = $request->validate([ 'lat' => ['required', 'numeric', 'between:-90,90'], 'lng' => ['required', 'numeric', 'between:-180,180'], 'address' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255'], ]); $store->update($data); ``` The same in a Django template: ```django {% load l10n %} ``` jQuery, Livewire (`wire:model`) and Alpine (`x-model`) listen on the bound inputs, which get native `input` and `change` events. jQuery `.serialize()` ignores custom elements, so use bound inputs or `new FormData(form)`. Style errors with `location-picker:state(interacted):invalid`. More in [docs/forms.md](docs/forms.md). ## Phone-first: field mode On a phone, a map in the middle of a checkout form gets in the way of scrolling. `presentation="field"` turns the picker into a compact form control: the chosen address (or the coordinates) and a **Choose on map** button. The map opens in a full-screen sheet with search, the locate button, **Confirm** and **Cancel**; the value changes only on Confirm. The map engine loads when the sheet first opens. ```html
``` - `auto` shows the field on touch screens up to 640 px wide (`(pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 640px)`) and the inline map elsewhere; `field` always shows the field; `inline` (the default) always shows the map. - Names, `FormData`, `required` and events are the same in every mode. Pans, search picks and locates inside the sheet are a draft: Confirm commits them (`input` then `change`, with their `source`); Cancel, Escape and `el.close()` change nothing and fire no `input`/`change`. - `el.showPicker()` opens the sheet, `el.close()` cancels it, and the `toggle` event (a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState`/`newState`) fires on open and close. - In field mode, `ready` and `el.map` wait for the first open. Do not gate the form on `el.ready`. - Add `search locate="button"`: field mode uses the same attributes as the inline map and adds nothing on its own. - A height you set on the element applies to the compact field too. Leave it off (the inline map is 320px tall by default), or set it in a `@media` rule that excludes phones. Use the inline map when the map is the content, or when the form is used on desktops. Use `auto` (or `field`) in checkout, delivery and sign-up forms that people fill in on phones. ## Frameworks Bind `value` (a `"lat,lng"` string) and update your state from `change`; `input` is for showing live updates. Do not write the value back from an `input` listener: in 3.0 that stops a pan in progress (Vue's `v-model` is fine). Spell configuration as HTML attributes (`lat-name`, `api-key`), which is SSR-safe. **Event names per framework.** The class callbacks `onChange`/`onInput`/`onAddressChange`/`onReady`/`onError` are options of the JavaScript class only. | Framework | `change` | `input` | `addresschange` | `ready` | `error` | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Plain JS | `addEventListener('change')` | `'input'` | `'addresschange'` | `'ready'` | `'error'` | | React 19 | `onChange` | `onInput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` (NOT `onError`: React's synthetic `error` never fires for this element; a type error in `jsx/react`) | | Vue 3 | `@change` | `@input` | `@addresschange` | `@ready` | `@error` | | Angular | `(change)` | `(input)` | `(addresschange)` | `(ready)` | `(error)` | | Svelte 5 | `onchange` | `oninput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` | | Solid | `on:change` | `on:input` | `on:addresschange` | `on:ready` | `on:error` | | Preact | `onchange` | `oninput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` | React's lowercase native handlers are attached on client render only. After `hydrateRoot`, use a ref (React hydration recipe below). Field mode's `toggle` event is `ontoggle` in React, Preact and Svelte, `@toggle` in Vue, `(toggle)` in Angular and `on:toggle` in Solid. ### React 19 / Next.js App Router ```tsx 'use client'; import 'location-picker'; // defines ; SSR-safe no-op on the server import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react'; // JSX typings import { useState } from 'react'; export function StoreLocationField({ initial = '' }: { initial?: string }) { const [value, setValue] = useState(initial); // "lat,lng" or "" // Attributes, value and onChange/onInput survive SSR hydration; objects (messages…) and onaddresschange go in a ref (see the React hydration recipe). return ( <> setValue(e.currentTarget.value)} style={{ height: 360 }} />

{value || 'Pan the map to choose'}

); } //
: formData.get('lat'), formData.get('lng'), formData.get('location') ``` **React hydration recipe.** With `hydrateRoot` (Next.js App Router, Remix), React applies neither object props (`messages`, `mapOptions`, `engine`, `geocoder`, `geolocation`, an adapter-object `provider`) nor the lowercase native handlers to custom elements. Set them in a ref callback; refs are attached on hydration. Attributes, `value` and `onChange`/`onInput` keep working. ```tsx 'use client'; import 'location-picker'; import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react'; import type { AddressDetail } from 'location-picker'; import { useState } from 'react'; export function AddressField() { const [address, setAddress] = useState(null); return ( <> { if (!el) return; el.messages = { locate: 'Use my position' }; const onAddress = (e: CustomEvent) => setAddress(e.detail.address); el.addEventListener('addresschange', onAddress); return () => el.removeEventListener('addresschange', onAddress); }} />

{address ?? 'No address yet'}

); } ``` ### Vue 3 ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite'; import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'location-picker' } } })], }); ``` ```vue ``` ### Angular 17+ (reactive forms, no custom ControlValueAccessor) ```ts import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from '@angular/core'; import { FormControl, FormGroup, ReactiveFormsModule, Validators } from '@angular/forms'; import 'location-picker'; @Component({ selector: 'app-store-form', standalone: true, imports: [ReactiveFormsModule], schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA], template: ` @if (form.controls.location.touched && form.controls.location.invalid) {

Choose a location.

} `, }) export class StoreFormComponent { form = new FormGroup({ location: new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true, validators: [Validators.required] }) }); save() { const [lat, lng] = this.form.getRawValue().location.split(',').map(Number); console.log({ lat, lng }); } } ``` Svelte 5, Solid, Preact, Nuxt, Astro, Livewire, Alpine, htmx and component tests in jsdom or happy-dom: [docs/frameworks.md](docs/frameworks.md). ## Reading the result | Event | `detail` | Fires | | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `change` | `{ value, lat, lng, source, zoom, address, accuracy?, place? }` | on every commit; de-duplicated; never for property writes, form reset or restore | | `input` | same as `change` | live while the user drags (at most once per frame), and with the final value before every `change` | | `addresschange` | `{ value, lat, lng, address, result }` | when the address for the current value resolves (`search` or `reverse-geocode`) | | `ready` | `{ provider, map }` | when the map is mounted, and again after each remount | | `error` | a `LocationPickerError` with `code`, `fix`, `level` | on asynchronous failures; logged with its fix unless you call `preventDefault()` | | `toggle` | a native `ToggleEvent` (`oldState`, `newState`) | field mode: when the map sheet opens or closes | Read the current state from properties: `el.value` (`"lat,lng"` or `""`), `el.valueAsLatLng` (`{ lat, lng }` or `null`), `el.address` and `el.map` (the engine map, after `ready`). `el.ready` is a promise for the mounted picker. ## Google Maps Google is used only when you ask for it: `provider="google"`, or `api-key`, `map-id` or `marker="advanced"`. Search then uses Google's `PlaceAutocompleteElement` and reverse geocoding uses the Google Geocoder, so Google results never appear on an OpenStreetMap map and vice versa. ```html
``` If the page already loads the Maps JavaScript API, `provider="google"` uses it and no key attribute is needed. Wheel and double-click zoom stay anchored at the pin; a pinch on Google Maps zooms around the fingers and commits the new centre. ## JavaScript class `LocationPicker` renders into an element you own (light DOM), for pages that do not use the custom element or that need the engine map synchronously. ```html
``` ```ts import * as L from 'leaflet'; import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css'; import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core'; // class only, no custom element import { leafletProvider } from 'location-picker/leaflet'; const picker = new LocationPicker('#map', { provider: leafletProvider({ engine: L }), value: '51.5074,-0.1278', zoom: 13, search: true, locate: 'button', latInput: '#lat', lngInput: '#lng', onChange: ({ lat, lng, source }) => console.log(source, lat, lng), }); L.circle(picker.valueAsLatLng!, { radius: 200 }).addTo(picker.map!); // synchronous: adapter object + engine present (never waits for CSS) // later (SPA route change): picker.destroy(); ``` Every option is also an element property and (for primitives) a kebab-case attribute: `latInput` = `lat-input`. Unknown option keys log a warning that lists the valid ones. ## Attributes | Attribute | Default | Notes | | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `value` | `""` (unset) | Initial value; lenient (`"48.8584, 2.2945"`, DMS, `geo:`, map URLs) | | `center`, `zoom` | world view `20,0`; zoom 15 with a value or center, else 2 | `center` is where the view starts while unset; it is never submitted | | `name`, `lat-name`, `lng-name`, `address-name` | `""` | FormData entries | | `lat-input`, `lng-input`, `value-input`, `address-input` | `""` | Existing inputs to fill (id or CSS selector) | | `required`, `disabled`, `readonly` | off | `readonly`: zoom allowed, the value cannot change | | `provider` | `leaflet` (`google` when `api-key` or `map-id` is set) | `leaflet`, `google` or `maplibre` | | `api-key`, `map-id` | `""` | Google only | | `tile-url`, `attribution` | OpenStreetMap tiles and credit | Leaflet raster tiles; use your own tiles in production | | `map-style` | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | MapLibre only | | `engine-url`, `engine-css-url` | `""` (automatic) | Engine JS and CSS to load: a URL, or `"none"` to never load them (you provide the engine) | | `search`, `placeholder` | off | Search box; typed or pasted coordinates jump directly, with no network call | | `reverse-geocode` | off | Look up the address after each commit (fires `addresschange`) | | `locate` | `off` | `button` (prompts only on click) or `auto` (also tries once on load while unset); `""` = `button` | | `marker` | `pin` | `none` hides the pin; `advanced` = Google AdvancedMarkerElement (needs `map-id`) | | `gesture-handling` | `auto` | `cooperative`, `greedy` or `none`; `auto` is cooperative (Ctrl/⌘ + wheel) when the page scrolls | | `max-zoom`, `precision` | 19 for OSM tiles; 6 decimals | | | `presentation` | `inline` | `field` (compact control, full-screen map sheet) or `auto` (field on phones); see field mode | | `webmcp` | off | Register experimental WebMCP tools for browser agents | Methods: `setLocation(lat, lng)` or `setLocation('lat,lng')` (commits with source `api`), `locate()` (geolocates, never hangs), `geocode(query)`, `lookupAddress()`, `showPicker()` and `close()` (field mode), plus the native `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()` and `setCustomValidity()`. Object properties (`messages`, `geocoder`, `engine`, `mapOptions`, `geolocation`) are set from JavaScript. Full list: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md). ## Styling The element renders into an open shadow root. Style it with CSS custom properties (`--lp-pin-color`, `--lp-pin-size`, `--lp-accent`, `--lp-tile-filter`, …), parts (`location-picker::part(pin)`), slots (`slot="marker"` for your own pin) and states (`location-picker:state(unset)`). It is 320px tall by default; set your own `height`. Dark mode follows `color-scheme`, and the layout uses logical properties for right-to-left pages. Field mode adds the parts `field`, `field-value`, `field-button`, `sheet`, `sheet-header` and `cancel-button` (Confirm is `confirm-button`) and the state `:state(open)`; its texts are the `chooseOnMap`, `fieldPlaceholder`, `cancel` and `confirm` keys of `messages`. ## Providers and usage policies - **OpenStreetMap tiles** (the default) come from `https://tile.openstreetmap.org` under the [OSM tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/): the "© OpenStreetMap contributors" attribution stays visible, and the service is best-effort with no SLA. For production traffic, use your own or a commercial tile server with `tile-url` and `attribution`. - **Search and reverse geocoding** on Leaflet and MapLibre use [Photon](https://photon.komoot.io/), which is free under fair use with no SLA. Requests are debounced (at least 300 ms on the public endpoint), cached and need 3 characters. For production, self-host Photon or use a commercial endpoint: `geocoder: photonGeocoder({ url })`, or your own geocoder. - **Google Maps** content stays on Google maps. The [Google Maps Platform Terms](https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) do not allow Google results on a non-Google map, so each provider gets its paired geocoder and a mismatch is refused with `GEOCODER_MISMATCH`. Switching providers clears the address. - **MapLibre** is bring-your-own (`maplibre-gl` and its CSS), with OpenFreeMap vector tiles by default. Nominatim is never a default and is not used by any example here. Before writing your own Nominatim geocoder, read its usage policy at https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/: it forbids client-side autocomplete and caps use at one request per second. Details, self-hosting and custom geocoders: [docs/providers.md](docs/providers.md). Content Security Policy recipes for each setup: [docs/csp.md](docs/csp.md). ## Common mistakes - **The unpinned v1 URL.** `https://unpkg.com/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js` (and the same path on jsDelivr) is the frozen v1 file forever: global `locationPicker`, Google Maps only, no `` element. For v3, load `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3` and keep the `@3`. - **Latitude first, no arrays.** Values are `"lat,lng"` strings or `{ lat, lng }` objects. Arrays are rejected because GeoJSON uses `[lng, lat]`. A swapped pair with both numbers in range (`"2.2945,48.8584"`) cannot be detected, so check the order. - **Choose Google explicitly.** Google Maps is used only with `provider="google"`, `api-key`, `map-id` or `marker="advanced"`. Otherwise the picker uses OpenStreetMap, even when `google.maps` is already loaded on the page. - **Put `required` on the picker,** never on hidden bound inputs. A hidden, empty, `required` input blocks the submit as "not focusable". - **jQuery `.serialize()` skips custom elements.** Use bound inputs (`lat-input`/`lng-input`) or `new FormData(form)`. - **`import 'location-picker'` defines the element.** `location-picker/core` is the class only and defines nothing, so importing only `core` leaves `` blank. - **Read results from `value` or `valueAsLatLng`,** not `getMarkerPosition()`. While the picker is unset, `getMarkerPosition()` returns the view centre (for example the 20,0 world view), not a chosen point. - **The `lat`/`lng` attributes are the initial value only.** Once the control is dirty (a pan, or the `el.value = ''` that `v-model` and `formControlName` write on mount), changing them is ignored with a warning. Bind `value="lat,lng"` or call `setLocation()`. - **React SSR (`hydrateRoot`: Next.js App Router, Remix):** React applies no object props (`messages`, `geocoder`, …) and no lowercase native handlers (`onaddresschange`, `onready`, `onerror`) during hydration. Set them in a ref callback (see the React hydration recipe). - **MapLibre CSS is yours to load:** `import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'`, or set `engine-css-url`. The library never fetches MapLibre or its CSS by default. - **The stylesheet path is `location-picker/style.css`.** `location-picker/dist/location-picker.css` is not exported. You only need it with `injectStyles: false`. Every runtime problem is reported with a stable code and a one-line fix, for example `[location-picker] … Fix: Add api-key="YOUR_KEY", or load the Google Maps JS API before the picker.` See [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md) and [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md). ## Upgrading from 1.x or 2.x The old script URL keeps working: `dist/location-picker.min.js` is a frozen copy of the v1 API (global `locationPicker`, Google Maps) with the longitude-wrap fix. npm users of 1.x change one import; 2.x Google code keeps a synchronous map with an adapter object: ```ts // 1.x npm code: one-line change, identical behaviour (frozen file) import locationPicker from 'location-picker/v1'; // 2.x Google code: keep a synchronous google.maps.Map with an adapter object import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core'; import { googleProvider } from 'location-picker/google'; const lp = new LocationPicker('map', { provider: googleProvider(), value: { lat: 45.5, lng: -73.56 }, onChange: (d) => console.log(d.lat, d.lng) }); google.maps.event.addListener(lp.map!, 'idle', () => console.log(lp.getMarkerPosition())); ``` Every v1 and v2 API, what changed and the one-line fixes: [docs/migration.md](docs/migration.md). ## Compatibility Browser, device and framework results are generated by the test matrix, never written by hand: see [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [compatibility page](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/compat/). ## Ask a person for a location: pick link `https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/pick/` is a hosted page that asks a person for an exact location with nothing to install: send the link from a chat bot, an AI agent, a support ticket or a no-code automation. The person moves the map (or searches, or taps "Use my location") and confirms. - Start it with `?lat=48.8584&lng=2.2945` (a starting point to confirm or adjust), `zoom` (1 to 19), `q=Eiffel Tower` (picks the first search result) and `lang`. - By default the page shows the result with copy buttons (decimal, DMS, `geo:` URI, Google Maps and OpenStreetMap links) and Web Share. - `redirect=https://example.com/done` sends the person there after a click, with `lat`, `lng` and (when known) `address` appended. Only `https://` URLs are accepted, and the page shows the destination host first. - `return=postmessage&origin=https://example.com` posts `{ type: 'location-picker:pick', lat, lng, address }` to the page that opened it (`window.open`) or embeds it (an iframe), only to that exact origin. `address` is `null` while unknown. - The page has no server, no storage, no cookies and no analytics; the state lives only in the URL. It uses OpenStreetMap and Photon. For heavy use, host your own copy: `node scripts/build-site.mjs` builds the static site (MIT) into `_site/`, with the page at `pick/`. readmeHtml:
location-picker

Let people pick an exact spot on a map, and get lat,lng in your form.

Form-ready map location picker: pan a map under a fixed pin to pick one latitude/longitude. Web component + class, keyless OpenStreetMap by default, Google and MapLibre optional.

!location-picker in a form: an OpenStreetMap map with a fixed red pin on the Eiffel Tower, a search box and a locate button, then a Save button and the value the form submits, location=48.85837,2.294481

Live demo · No-code embed · Pick link · [API reference](docs/api.md) · [For AI agents](#for-ai-agents) · MIT

One script tag, no API key, no build step. Put the element inside your form:

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>

<form method="post" action="/places">

  <label for="where">Location</label>

  <location-picker id="where" search locate="button" name="location" required></location-picker>

  <button>Save</button>

</form>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

People pan the map under the pin, search for a place, paste coordinates or tap the locate button (the browser asks for permission only then). On Save, the form posts location=48.85837,2.294481, latitude first, like any other field. In JavaScript, read the element's value or listen for change: e.detail has value, lat, lng, source and address.

  • With npm: npm i location-picker, then import 'location-picker'. Recipes for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and more: [Frameworks](#frameworks).
  • With a coding agent: npx skills add cyphercodes/location-picker adds the location-picker Agent Skill (it also ships in the package, at node_modules/location-picker/skills/location-picker/SKILL.md). llms.txt is the short version of these docs, and [Common mistakes](#common-mistakes) lists the traps.
  • Without code: the embed generator writes the snippet for WordPress, Webflow, Squarespace, Shopify or a plain HTML form ([per-platform guide](docs/embed.md)).
  • To ask a person: send them the pick link. They confirm a point on a map with nothing to install, and you get it back as text they copy to you, an https:// redirect after their click, or a postMessage to your origin ([how it works](#ask-a-person-for-a-location-pick-link)). Made for chat bots, AI agents and support tickets. Try /pick/?q=Eiffel Tower.

Why location-picker

Use it when a form needs one precise point: a store, branch or sensor location in an admin screen, a delivery or pickup pin at checkout, an event venue, the place of a report, a home or work location in a profile.

  • A real form field. required validates, form reset works and back/forward navigation restores it. Submit one "lat,lng" entry (name), separate entries (lat-name, lng-name), or fill inputs you already have (lat-input, lng-input). See [Forms](#forms).
  • No API key to start. OpenStreetMap through Leaflet by default; Google Maps or MapLibre when you choose them. The default OpenStreetMap tiles and Photon address search are free public services with no SLA: for production traffic, use your own or a commercial tile server and geocoder ([usage policies](#providers-and-usage-policies)).
  • Pan, search, paste or locate. Arrow keys and Enter work too, and the locate button asks for permission only when clicked. Typed or pasted coordinates jump straight there with no network call: 48.8584, 2.2945, DMS, geo: URIs and Google, OpenStreetMap or Apple Maps links.
  • Phone-first when you want it. [Field mode](#phone-first-field-mode) shows a compact control that opens the map full screen; the value changes only on Confirm.
  • Your stack. Plain HTML forms and server templates (Laravel, Django, Rails), React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid and Preact; jQuery, Livewire, Alpine and htmx through bound inputs. TypeScript types and JSX typings are included.
  • No runtime npm dependencies. Leaflet, MapLibre and the Google Maps types are optional peers. When the page has no Leaflet, it is loaded from jsDelivr ([Install](#install)).
  • Clear errors, generated test results. Every runtime problem has a stable code and a one-line fix ([error codes](docs/errors.md)). Browser and device results come from the test matrix: [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md).

When not to use it: drawing shapes, routes or areas; several markers; a full mapping application (use Leaflet, MapLibre or the Google Maps JS API directly); text-only address autocomplete with no map; offline maps; React Native or other native mobile apps.

Install

| How | Use |

| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Script tag (no bundler) | <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script> |

| npm | npm i location-picker, then import 'location-picker' |

| npm, class only | import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core' (defines no element) |

| Upgrading 1.x code | import locationPicker from 'location-picker/v1' ([migration guide](docs/migration.md)) |

The script tag defines <location-picker> and sets window.LocationPicker (the class, with every export as a static). https://unpkg.com/location-picker@3 serves the same file. Keep the @3: the unpinned /dist/location-picker.min.js path is the frozen v1 file. In ES modules from a CDN, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3/+esm defines the element too.

Leaflet 1.9.4 is loaded on demand from jsDelivr with Subresource Integrity, only when window.L is absent. Bundler users can pass their own Leaflet instead (see [the JavaScript class](#javascript-class)).

To watch the value change while you try it, here is a complete page:

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


<!doctype html>

<html lang="en">

<meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

<title>Pick a location</title>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>

<label for="where">Where is it?</label>

<location-picker id="where" search locate="button" style="height: 400px"></location-picker>

<p>Picked: <output id="out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script>

  document.getElementById('where').addEventListener('change', (e) => {

    document.getElementById('out').textContent = e.detail.value; // "48.85837,2.294481"; e.detail has lat, lng, source, address

  });

</script>

</html>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

How the value works

  • The picker starts unset (value === "") unless you give it a value. While unset, the map shows center (or a world view) and the pin is dimmed.
  • The user commits a point by panning the map, using the arrow keys, pressing Enter on the map, clicking the confirm button (shown while unset when center is set), picking a search result, or locating. setLocation() commits too.
  • Zooming never changes the value: zoom is anchored at the pin.
  • Every commit fires input (final value), then change, with detail.source: user, api, geolocation or search. Live input events fire while the user drags.
  • Writing el.value = '48.8584,2.2945' is silent (no events), like a native <input>.
  • The value string is always latitude first, dot decimal, no spaces, rounded to precision decimals (6 by default): "48.85837,2.294481".

Forms

The element is form-associated: it validates with required, resets with the form and restores on back/forward navigation. Choose what it submits:

| Attributes | Submitted entries |

| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |

| name="loc" | loc=48.85837,2.294481 |

| lat-name="lat" lng-name="lng" | lat=48.85837, lng=2.294481 |

| + address-name="addr" | addr=<address> ("" while unknown) |

| lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" (bound inputs) | your existing inputs submit themselves; the picker fills them |

The recommended server-rendered pattern puts the inputs inside the element. Without JavaScript they are visible and typed by hand; with it they are hidden, filled by the map, and still submitted. Their server values seed the picker, and a form reset brings them back.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


<form method="POST" action="{{ route('stores.update', $store) }}">

  @csrf

  @method('PUT')

  <label for="store-location">Store location</label>

  <location-picker id="store-location" lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" address-name="address"

                   required search reverse-geocode style="height: 360px">

    {{-- Without JS these are visible and typed by hand. With JS they are hidden, filled by the map, and still submitted.

         Their values seed the picker. No `required` here: the picker validates. --}}

    <input id="lat" name="lat" inputmode="decimal" value="{{ old('lat', $store->lat) }}" aria-label="Latitude">

    <input id="lng" name="lng" inputmode="decimal" value="{{ old('lng', $store->lng) }}" aria-label="Longitude">

  </location-picker>

  @error('lat') <p class="error">{{ $message }}</p> @enderror

  <button type="submit">Save</button>

</form>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

$store->update($data);

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

The same in a Django template:

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


{% load l10n %}

<location-picker lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" required search>

  <input id="lat" name="lat" value="{{ form.lat.value|default_if_none:''|unlocalize }}" aria-label="Latitude">

  <input id="lng" name="lng" value="{{ form.lng.value|default_if_none:''|unlocalize }}" aria-label="Longitude">

</location-picker>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

jQuery, Livewire (wire:model) and Alpine (x-model) listen on the bound inputs, which get native input and change events. jQuery .serialize() ignores custom elements, so use bound inputs or new FormData(form). Style errors with location-picker:state(interacted):invalid. More in [docs/forms.md](docs/forms.md).

Phone-first: field mode

On a phone, a map in the middle of a checkout form gets in the way of scrolling. presentation="field" turns the picker into a compact form control: the chosen address (or the coordinates) and a Choose on map button. The map opens in a full-screen sheet with search, the locate button, Confirm and Cancel; the value changes only on Confirm. The map engine loads when the sheet first opens.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


<form method="post" action="/deliveries">

  <label for="drop">Delivery spot</label>

  <location-picker id="drop" presentation="auto" name="location" search locate="button" reverse-geocode required></location-picker>

  <button>Continue</button>

</form>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

  • auto shows the field on touch screens up to 640 px wide ((pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 640px)) and the inline map elsewhere; field always shows the field; inline (the default) always shows the map.
  • Names, FormData, required and events are the same in every mode. Pans, search picks and locates inside the sheet are a draft: Confirm commits them (input then change, with their source); Cancel, Escape and el.close() change nothing and fire no input/change.
  • el.showPicker() opens the sheet, el.close() cancels it, and the toggle event (a ToggleEvent with oldState/newState) fires on open and close.
  • In field mode, ready and el.map wait for the first open. Do not gate the form on el.ready.
  • Add search locate="button": field mode uses the same attributes as the inline map and adds nothing on its own.
  • A height you set on the element applies to the compact field too. Leave it off (the inline map is 320px tall by default), or set it in a @media rule that excludes phones.

Use the inline map when the map is the content, or when the form is used on desktops. Use auto (or field) in checkout, delivery and sign-up forms that people fill in on phones.

Frameworks

Bind value (a "lat,lng" string) and update your state from change; input is for showing live updates. Do not write the value back from an input listener: in 3.0 that stops a pan in progress (Vue's v-model is fine). Spell configuration as HTML attributes (lat-name, api-key), which is SSR-safe.

Event names per framework. The class callbacks onChange/onInput/onAddressChange/onReady/onError are options of the JavaScript class only.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

| Framework | change | input | addresschange | ready | error |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Plain JS | addEventListener('change') | 'input' | 'addresschange' | 'ready' | 'error' |

| React 19 | onChange | onInput | onaddresschange | onready | onerror (NOT onError: React's synthetic error never fires for this element; a type error in jsx/react) |

| Vue 3 | @change | @input | @addresschange | @ready | @error |

| Angular | (change) | (input) | (addresschange) | (ready) | (error) |

| Svelte 5 | onchange | oninput | onaddresschange | onready | onerror |

| Solid | on:change | on:input | on:addresschange | on:ready | on:error |

| Preact | onchange | oninput | onaddresschange | onready | onerror |

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

React's lowercase native handlers are attached on client render only. After hydrateRoot, use a ref (React hydration recipe below). Field mode's toggle event is ontoggle in React, Preact and Svelte, @toggle in Vue, (toggle) in Angular and on:toggle in Solid.

'use client';

import 'location-picker';                          // defines <location-picker>; SSR-safe no-op on the server

import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react';   // JSX typings

import { useState } from 'react';



export function StoreLocationField({ initial = '' }: { initial?: string }) {

  const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);    // "lat,lng" or ""

  // Attributes, value and onChange/onInput survive SSR hydration; objects (messages…) and onaddresschange go in a ref (see the React hydration recipe).

  return (

    <>

      <label htmlFor="loc">Location</label>

      <location-picker id="loc" name="location" lat-name="lat" lng-name="lng" required search

        value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.currentTarget.value)} style={{ height: 360 }} />

  );

}

// <form action={saveStore}>: formData.get('lat'), formData.get('lng'), formData.get('location')

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

React hydration recipe. With hydrateRoot (Next.js App Router, Remix), React applies neither object props (messages, mapOptions, engine, geocoder, geolocation, an adapter-object provider) nor the lowercase native handlers to custom elements. Set them in a ref callback; refs are attached on hydration. Attributes, value and onChange/onInput keep working.


'use client';

import 'location-picker';

import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react';

import type { AddressDetail } from 'location-picker';

import { useState } from 'react';



export function AddressField() {

  const [address, setAddress] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (

    <>

      <location-picker

        name="location"

        reverse-geocode

        ref={(el) => {

          if (!el) return;

          el.messages = { locate: 'Use my position' };

          const onAddress = (e: CustomEvent<AddressDetail>) => setAddress(e.detail.address);

          el.addEventListener('addresschange', onAddress);

          return () => el.removeEventListener('addresschange', onAddress);

        }}

      />

      <p>{address ?? 'No address yet'}</p>

    </>

  );

}

Svelte 5, Solid, Preact, Nuxt, Astro, Livewire, Alpine, htmx and component tests in jsdom or happy-dom: [docs/frameworks.md](docs/frameworks.md).

Reading the result

| Event | detail | Fires |

| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| change | { value, lat, lng, source, zoom, address, accuracy?, place? } | on every commit; de-duplicated; never for property writes, form reset or restore |

| input | same as change | live while the user drags (at most once per frame), and with the final value before every change |

| addresschange | { value, lat, lng, address, result } | when the address for the current value resolves (search or reverse-geocode) |

| ready | { provider, map } | when the map is mounted, and again after each remount |

| error | a LocationPickerError with code, fix, level | on asynchronous failures; logged with its fix unless you call preventDefault() |

| toggle | a native ToggleEvent (oldState, newState) | field mode: when the map sheet opens or closes |

Read the current state from properties: el.value ("lat,lng" or ""), el.valueAsLatLng ({ lat, lng } or null), el.address and el.map (the engine map, after ready). el.ready is a promise for the mounted picker.

Google Maps

Google is used only when you ask for it: provider="google", or api-key, map-id or marker="advanced". Search then uses Google's PlaceAutocompleteElement and reverse geocoding uses the Google Geocoder, so Google results never appear on an OpenStreetMap map and vice versa.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->


<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>

<!-- Restrict the key by HTTP referrer. Enable Maps JavaScript API + Places API (New); Geocoding API only for reverse-geocode. -->

<form method="post" action="/checkout/address">

  <label for="drop">Drop-off point</label>

  <location-picker id="drop" provider="google" api-key="YOUR_BROWSER_KEY" name="dropoff" address-name="dropoff_address"

                   search reverse-geocode locate="button" required center="40.7128,-74.0060" style="height: 420px"></location-picker>

  <button>Continue</button>

</form>

<script>

  const drop = document.getElementById('drop');

  drop.addEventListener('change', (e) => console.log(e.detail.lat, e.detail.lng, e.detail.source));

  drop.addEventListener('error', (e) => console.log(e.detail.code, e.detail.fix)); // e.g. GOOGLE_AUTH_FAILED; also logged

  drop.addEventListener('ready', (e) => console.log('google.maps.Map:', e.detail.map)); // no unhandled rejection on failure

</script>

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

If the page already loads the Maps JavaScript API, provider="google" uses it and no key attribute is needed. Wheel and double-click zoom stay anchored at the pin; a pinch on Google Maps zooms around the fingers and commits the new centre.

JavaScript class

LocationPicker renders into an element you own (light DOM), for pages that do not use the custom element or that need the engine map synchronously.

import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css';

import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core';        // class only, no custom element

import { leafletProvider } from 'location-picker/leaflet';



const picker = new LocationPicker<L.Map>('#map', {

  provider: leafletProvider<L.Map>({ engine: L }),

  value: '51.5074,-0.1278',

  zoom: 13,

  search: true,

  locate: 'button',

  latInput: '#lat',

  lngInput: '#lng',

  onChange: ({ lat, lng, source }) => console.log(source, lat, lng),

});

L.circle(picker.valueAsLatLng!, { radius: 200 }).addTo(picker.map!);   // synchronous: adapter object + engine present (never waits for CSS)

// later (SPA route change): picker.destroy();

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

Every option is also an element property and (for primitives) a kebab-case attribute: latInput = lat-input. Unknown option keys log a warning that lists the valid ones.

Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Notes |

| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| value | "" (unset) | Initial value; lenient ("48.8584, 2.2945", DMS, geo:, map URLs) |

| center, zoom | world view 20,0; zoom 15 with a value or center, else 2 | center is where the view starts while unset; it is never submitted |

| name, lat-name, lng-name, address-name | "" | FormData entries |

| lat-input, lng-input, value-input, address-input | "" | Existing inputs to fill (id or CSS selector) |

| required, disabled, readonly | off | readonly: zoom allowed, the value cannot change |

| provider | leaflet (google when api-key or map-id is set) | leaflet, google or maplibre |

| api-key, map-id | "" | Google only |

| tile-url, attribution | OpenStreetMap tiles and credit | Leaflet raster tiles; use your own tiles in production |

| map-style | https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty | MapLibre only |

| engine-url, engine-css-url | "" (automatic) | Engine JS and CSS to load: a URL, or "none" to never load them (you provide the engine) |

| search, placeholder | off | Search box; typed or pasted coordinates jump directly, with no network call |

| reverse-geocode | off | Look up the address after each commit (fires addresschange) |

| locate | off | button (prompts only on click) or auto (also tries once on load while unset); "" = button |

| marker | pin | none hides the pin; advanced = Google AdvancedMarkerElement (needs map-id) |

| gesture-handling | auto | cooperative, greedy or none; auto is cooperative (Ctrl/⌘ + wheel) when the page scrolls |

| max-zoom, precision | 19 for OSM tiles; 6 decimals | |

| presentation | inline | field (compact control, full-screen map sheet) or auto (field on phones); see field mode |

| webmcp | off | Register experimental WebMCP tools for browser agents |

Methods: setLocation(lat, lng) or setLocation('lat,lng') (commits with source api), locate() (geolocates, never hangs), geocode(query), lookupAddress(), showPicker() and close() (field mode), plus the native checkValidity(), reportValidity() and setCustomValidity(). Object properties (messages, geocoder, engine, mapOptions, geolocation) are set from JavaScript. Full list: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md).

Styling

The element renders into an open shadow root. Style it with CSS custom properties (--lp-pin-color, --lp-pin-size, --lp-accent, --lp-tile-filter, …), parts (location-picker::part(pin)), slots (slot="marker" for your own pin) and states (location-picker:state(unset)). It is 320px tall by default; set your own height. Dark mode follows color-scheme, and the layout uses logical properties for right-to-left pages. Field mode adds the parts field, field-value, field-button, sheet, sheet-header and cancel-button (Confirm is confirm-button) and the state :state(open); its texts are the chooseOnMap, fieldPlaceholder, cancel and confirm keys of messages.

Providers and usage policies

  • OpenStreetMap tiles (the default) come from https://tile.openstreetmap.org under the OSM tile usage policy: the "© OpenStreetMap contributors" attribution stays visible, and the service is best-effort with no SLA. For production traffic, use your own or a commercial tile server with tile-url and attribution.
  • Search and reverse geocoding on Leaflet and MapLibre use Photon, which is free under fair use with no SLA. Requests are debounced (at least 300 ms on the public endpoint), cached and need 3 characters. For production, self-host Photon or use a commercial endpoint: geocoder: photonGeocoder({ url }), or your own geocoder.
  • Google Maps content stays on Google maps. The Google Maps Platform Terms do not allow Google results on a non-Google map, so each provider gets its paired geocoder and a mismatch is refused with GEOCODER_MISMATCH. Switching providers clears the address.

Common mistakes

  • The unpinned v1 URL. https://unpkg.com/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js (and the same path on jsDelivr) is the frozen v1 file forever: global locationPicker, Google Maps only, no <location-picker> element. For v3, load https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3 and keep the @3.
  • Latitude first, no arrays. Values are "lat,lng" strings or { lat, lng } objects. Arrays are rejected because GeoJSON uses [lng, lat]. A swapped pair with both numbers in range ("2.2945,48.8584") cannot be detected, so check the order.

  • Put required on the picker, never on hidden bound inputs. A hidden, empty, required input blocks the submit as "not focusable".
